seed: A motion that changes a layer's COLOUR has two colours to choose, From and To, and they used to be the only two colours in the panel that opened the Mac's own colour window: no shades, no colours out of the document, and none of the colours you had saved. This walk saves a colour called Brand off a shape's Fill, adds a Colour motion to that shape, then drives both wells through the app's own picker, which is the proof on its own: a walk can press the app's picker and cannot touch the system colour panel at all. Then To is driven a second time from the saved colours mark beside the well, by name. Both ends are put on colours of their own first, because the motion starts with both on the layer's own crimson and Brand IS that crimson: picking it straight away would be picking the colour already there. Both rows say the colour they are holding out loud, so each pick is read straight back, and one undo per pick puts it back.

steps.comment: The saved-colour menu takes the name of the row it sits on. In the Effects list a border's colour has a row of its own called Color; in Appearance the swatch sits on the Fill row itself, so this menu is Fill.

steps.note: the shape is crimson and that crimson is saved as Brand, so there is a saved colour for the motion rows to offer

steps.comment: The motion's own row, the line that reads the colour change back as a sentence. The section it sits in is called Color and carries no readout of its own.

steps.note: a Colour motion, starting where the layer already is. Both ends are the app's own swatch now, not the system colour well that used to sit here.

THE TEST: the From well opens the one picker every other colour row opens. A walk can see and press the app's own picker and cannot touch the system colour panel at all, so pressing a swatch inside this one is the whole proof.
the blue typed into the picker landed on From, and the row says so

steps.comment: To is put on a green of its own FIRST, so that picking the saved colour next is a real change rather than the colour it is already holding. Adding the motion starts both ends on the layer's own crimson, and Brand IS that crimson, so a walk that went straight to the saved menu picked what was already there and proved nothing: the undo after it took back the From pick instead, and read as a no-op.

steps.note: both ends have now been driven through the app's own picker: From is blue, To is green, and neither touched the Mac's colour window
THE TEST: beside the To well sits the same swatchpalette mark every other colour row wears, with Brand on it by name. Not offering the saved colours here was the whole complaint.
To is the saved crimson, and the row's summary reads the pair back: blue to crimson

steps.comment: one undo takes back the saved-colour pick and no more, so To is the green it was holding a moment ago.

steps.note: one undo per pick: choosing a colour is one step, not one step per frame of the slider, and it takes back the To pick alone

steps.comment: and the one before that takes back the green typed into the picker, leaving To on the crimson it started at.

steps.note: a third undo puts From back, so all three picks were a single step each and the motion is where it started
